utterances.text: -- go through with Mr. Krajisnik. I have another conference with Mr. Krajisnik this afternoon and tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me put it very short. I apologise for interrupting. There are no further witnesses scheduled for this week. If you say I need two days, then you would have to start on Thursday because the Chamber, as you may have noticed earlier, is not very much inclined to meet demands of further preparation although the events now give you an opportunity to further prepare. If you say, "I would need six hours or five hours," then I'm inclined to allow you -- to give those hours but to schedule the beginning of the cross-examination accordingly so that we would finish by next Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I understand Your Honour's query in that sense. Of course I am not, today, in a position to say, "My cross-examination will be exactly four hours or I will need more than Friday for my cross-examination." Perhaps, Your Honour, I will be -- I would be hopeful that I could go from the beginning to the end of my cross-examination in one day, that being Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If I form a view that I may need a little bit more additional time, then perhaps if I could inform Your Honours tomorrow that a session on Thursday may be necessary as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's as much guidance as I can give at this moment because I'm still midway through my conferences with Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a very practical solution although your assessment at this moment is that you would need Friday only. I hardly dare to say that whether there would be any time left for questions by the Judges but -- and perhaps re-examination, so even if you say, I would finish in one day, we might have to start anyhow on Thursday, because we have to take all that into consideration. But you'll inform us in a bit more detail tomorrow, and then not in court, I take it, because we will then not schedule a hearing. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, our preference is that there be sufficient time allotted for the possibility of redirect examination. I don't want to find this butting up to the end of the day on Friday with absolutely no opportunity to have redirect examination and therefore inconveniencing Dr. Djokanovic to stay over the weekend. I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll do the following. Tomorrow we'll hear from Ms. Loukas or later today, we'll hear from Ms. Loukas how much time she would need. We'll keep on the safe side. We would include -- well let's say one hour for re-examination, according to the experience, that should be enough, and then perhaps add perhaps some time for the Judges as well. So that if you would say four hours, we would reserve six hours. If you would say three hours, we might reserve four and a half. So just to adapt more or less to the time that you would need. Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm much obliged. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a practical solution of the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Krajisnik would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before Mr. Krajisnik stands and addresses the Chamber, perhaps it would be good to excuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It depends on whether there's anything to be said in the presence of the witness. I don't think so, Mr. Krajisnik. Usually it's better to address these kinds of issues in the absence of the witness. Mr. Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, it's in Your Honour's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djokanovic, if you may have observed from the discussion we just had, it's a little bit uncertain when we would restart. You will be informed about it and you should make yourself available to the Victims and Witness Section, whether it would be Thursday and at what time on Thursday. It's unlikely, as far as I see it now, that we would restart tomorrow. Most likely it would start in the morning hours. So if you would -- if you could live with this uncertainty, I'd like you to instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you had given until now and you're still about to give during the rest of the week. You may have also noticed that this Chamber would prefer to finish your examination this week so that you can return home. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Djokanovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Honourable Trial Chamber to allow me, if necessary, to put some questions to this witness. I promise that I will do my best, together with my counsel, Ms. Loukas, to make an arrangement for her to put all the questions to the witness. However, if there are several important questions that need to be put by me that I be allowed to put questions to him because of the evidence that can be given by this witness in view of the reasons that I had already set out to this Honourable Chamber earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the Chamber gave once a ruling that although, as a rule, questions should be put to the witness by counsel, that not under all circumstances, the Chamber would disallow the accused to put some additional questions to the witness and always on the understanding that counsel would be consulted. Therefore, I take it that whether it finally comes to a request to put any questions to the witness, it first have to wait until you have discussed the matter with counsel, we first have to wait what questions will be put by counsel. As you already indicated, you try to give all your questions to counsel and if we would then finally end up in a situation where you would say one or two questions would still be needed in addition to that, we'll give counsel an opportunity to express whether there's any objection or to further consult with you at that very moment. But that was the ruling and I think that has not changed even though, finally, it never came to the point where you have put questions to the witness. We have not, under all circumstances, disallowed you to do it. Ms. Loukas. Do you remember the ruling, otherwise I could give you the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed to say one other thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although I have to ask you, we are quite late as a matter of fact. Mr. Krajisnik, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means. You had occasion to see what the previous two witnesses -- that they were very important but my counsel prepared my defence well and I did not want to push the matters. Ms. Loukas has been prepared well for the previous witnesses and whenever it's not necessary, I will not draw upon this privilege that you have given me but for a question for two. However, an issue might arise after the cross-examination conducted by my counsel, but since I'm unable to consult with my counsel, I simply cannot allow for the witness to leave before I put these questions to him. But you have to understand that witnesses are appearing before this Trial Chamber that can be of great help to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand your point. Ms. Loukas, perhaps the Chamber should pay a little bit more attention to possibilities for communication between counsel and the accused, even during the hearing so -- or during the very short break.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's clearly an issue that that question of communication and the question of interpretation during that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any further submissions?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I note the time. There's just one aspect. It seems to me that if the Trial Chamber does wish to ensure that there is enough time to complete this witness by Friday afternoon, and taking into account time for questions from Your Honours, time for re-examination, perhaps the most sensible option might be to commence on say Thursday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Afternoon might be -- we have the courtroom in the morning. That would mean that we have to start somewhere halfway in the morning. I do understand on the basis of your assessment, that you would take four hours if we take two hours in addition to that that would take six hours, and counting back from Friday, that would bring us somewhere at Thursday, well, let's say, at 10.30 or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course my four hours is a very provisional assessment at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, we'll adjourn until next Thursday at a time to be determined at a later stage once we have received information from Ms. Loukas on the time she would need for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although at an unknown time, the courtroom will be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.00 p.m.,
